#3292. The Hunger Games Meets The Walking Dead In This 40-Episode Sci-Fi Thriller Series

On paper, The Hunger Games and The Walking Dead are two distinct franchises. But picture a dystopian world where the apocalypse is not ruled by zombies but by monstrous humans themselves. Even the games they play among themselves to increase their class divides are more political and terrifying. There lies the premise of a compelling 40-episode sci-fi thriller.

Loosely based on the French graphic novel Le Transperceneige and Bong Joon Ho's movie of the same name, Snowpiercer has a distinct post-apocalyptic setup. Some shows, like The Walking Dead, are open world survival thrillers. Others, like Silo, unfold in underground bunkers. Snowpiercer primarily takes place in a titular train that endlessly circles Earth.

Finding shelter in a constantly moving train does not sound too bad when the planet outside is frozen beyond repair. In Snowpiercer's world, however, the man-made divides and horrors inside the train are far more disturbing than the thought of freezing to death. Owing to this, it seems fair to compare Snowpiercer with both The Hunger Games and The Walking Dead.

Panem, in The Hunger Games, weaponizes spectacle and controlled scarcity to exploit the lower classes. They quietly aggravate the existing divides between oppressed districts while ensuring the Capitol remains safe and sound. A similar system can be noticed in Snowpiercer. Just like Panem's districts in The Hunger Games are numbered based on economics, humanity is divided through a train's cars in Snowpiercer.

While the elite accommodate the front cars of the trains and enjoy every luxury, the ones at the back rot in inhumane conditions. Much like President Snow in The Hunger Games, the train's creator, Wilford, also has a cult-like following where he is almost treated like an overarching deity. Similar to Jennifer Lawrence's Katniss Everdeen, Snowpiercer also finds its reluctant rebel in Andre Layton.

He emerges from the depths of the lower classes but, like Katniss, realizes that overthrowing a tyrant is far easier than leading a deeply divided population without becoming a tyrant yourself.

Similar to the characters in The Walking Dead, the ones in Snowpiecer, too, gradually experience moral erosion in their post-apocalyptic world. Alliances keep shifting, and, instead of uniting against one common evil, the people get lost in their own petty conflicts and selfish desire to survive. Despite these overlaps, though, Snowpiercer finds its distinct voice through its detective noir drama.

Overall, Bong Joon Ho's Snowpiercer is an absolute masterpiece. The show does not even come close to being as gripping and intense as the award-winning film. However, the series still makes good use of its long runtime to expand the world-building from the movie. While the movie quickly moves from one car to another, the show carefully reveals how everything from water supply to food production works.

Instead of jumping from one action set piece to another, the show paces itself and introduces gripping mysteries to keep viewers hooked. The movie is star-studded, with Chris Evans, Tilda Swinton, Ed Harris, Song Kang-ho, Jamie Bell, and Octavia Spencer serving as its leads. Even the show, however, boasts memorable performances from Jennifer Connelly, Daveed Diggs, Rowan Blanchard, and Sean Bean.

All in all, the Snowpiercer show never comes off as a forced extension of the original movie. It also does not try too hard to draw any connections to the film, which helps it etch its own solid identity like The Hunger Games and The Walking Dead.

Snowpiercer is set aboard a perpetually moving train that carries the last survivors of humanity after Earth is frozen into an uninhabitable wasteland. As passengers remain divided by a rigid class system, former detective Andre Layton is drawn into a murder investigation that exposes growing unrest and ignites a struggle over who should control the future of the train.

That’s the idea behind LiberNovo’s ergonomic chairs, which combine support that moves with you and a choice of sizes, including the Maxis range for bigger and taller users. For Black Friday, LiberNovo is taking up to 42% off in the U.S., with chairs starting at $609 and offers running November 19–30.

Adjusting a chair for your desk is one thing. Keeping that support as you change position is another. LiberNovo’s Dynamic Support System links the neck support, backrest, armrests, and seat so they move together as you recline.

The Bionic FlexFit Backrest adds eight flexible panels that contour independently. Rather than relying on a single rigid backrest, the design lets different sections follow your back as you shift or turn. Once you’ve adjusted the chair to fit, the system is designed to maintain contact through those movements with fewer manual readjustments.

Both the Omni and Maxis families offer five recline positions: 105, 115, 125, 135, and 160 degrees. That gives you options for desk work, a more relaxed position for watching a video, and a deeper recline for a break.

A higher weight limit is only part of finding a chair that fits. Taller users also need enough seat depth, a headrest that reaches the right spot, and armrests with room to adjust.

The LiberNovo Maxis range addresses those details with a 52 cm seat depth, a wider backrest with a flared base, and an extended-travel headrest with 140 mm of vertical adjustment and 120 mm of front-to-back adjustment. There are three feature tiers in each family. Omni SE and Maxis Manual offer manually adjusted lumbar support, without a motor or battery. Both retain the flexible backrest, dynamic support, and five recline positions.

Omni Pro and Maxis Airflow add Active AirFlow seat ventilation. A fan draws air through the cushion to carry heat away, and an occupancy sensor pauses the fan when you stand up. These models also include a larger 3,000 mAh rechargeable battery.

#3288. WhatsApp is raising group chat limit to 1,500 participants

WhatsApp is gradually rolling out an increase to its group chat limit, allowing up to 1,500 participants to join in, instead of the previous 1,024 cap. Here are the details.

While there are exceptions, there are generally two kinds of WhatsApp users: those who hate group chats, and those who can’t seem to be in enough of them.

If you’re in the second category, you’re likely aware that WhatsApp has steadily increased the number of participants allowed in group chats over the years, jumping from 100 to 256 in 2016, then to 512 and, soon after, to 1,024 in 2022.

Now, as spotted by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is once again expanding that limit, raising the maximum number of participants in a group chat to 1,500.

According to the website, the new limit is rolling out to users on iOS and Android, though the rollout is gradual, meaning “not every account will see the higher limit immediately.”

WhatsApp is automatically updating existing groups to support the new limit. This means that admins do not need to take any action to unlock the higher capacity. As soon as the update becomes available to their accounts, their groups will support up to 1500 members. As a result, the update lets admins add up to 476 new members to their existing groups.

This rollout comes as WhatsApp has been working to make group chats easier to manage. Just last month, the company announced four new features, including the ability to pin messages indefinitely, share status updates within groups, filter conversations by mentions and replies, and share recent message history with new members after they join.

To read WABetaInfo’s full report, follow this link.

#3285. There's Actually a Simple Explanation for All These Widespread Outages

It feels like every time you look at your phone lately, another company is having an outage. Last week, there was Microsoft, whose outage took down services from Outlook to Teams. Then, the FAA grounded all flights across the U.S. following "communication issues." This week, a number of banks experienced outages, as did Apple. Even the NSA's internal communications network went dark. Some of the biggest corporations and organizations in the world can't seem to keep their services running, leading to widespread disruptions and confusion. When it's a one-off, it's an annoyance; when it's outage after outage, it starts to feel like a pattern.

That pattern, in turn, has begun to fuel anxiety among the general public. What could possibly be causing Apple, Microsoft, JP Morgan Chase, and the NSA alike to go dark at roughly the same time? Is it a coordinated cyberattack? An AI revolt? Is the end finally nigh? To an outside observer, it certainly appears like something coordinated and nefarious is happening here. Secretary of State Marco Rubio is insistent that there is "zero evidence" that hackers or bad actors caused any of these outages, and President Trump is particularly unconcerned by the whole ordeal, saying, "It's life," and "Things like that happen."

But to skeptics of the U.S. government, these trickles of information aren't necessarily reassuring. While I agree with calls for someone from the government (perhaps the president himself) to make an official announcement explaining the situation, the root cause does appear to be clear at this time: The short answer? AI is at fault here, but not in the way you think.

Love it or hate it, AI is a force to be reckoned with. While you might know that AI can generate hyper-realistic videos and manage your emails on your behalf, certain models are adept at discovering new security vulnerabilities in software. These models aren't just helpful tools; they far surpass the abilities of human researchers. You might remember Anthropic initially pulled the brakes on its breakthrough model, Claude Mythos, when it found that the model could root out security vulnerabilities in just about anything.

Mythos, and models like it, are a double-edged sword. On the one hand, they can be major assets for developers and researchers to find new security vulnerabilities that humans otherwise wouldn't have discovered, and patch them accordingly. Unfortunately, the same can be said for bad actors, who can use these models to learn about new security flaws and attempt to exploit them before researchers have a chance to find them. As such, software developers across the spectrum, from small-time devs to major corporations, have been racing to patch as many security vulnerabilities as they can find—and they're finding a lot.

You might notice your PC's security updates, for example, are shipping with more patches than usual—historic levels, even. Microsoft keeps breaking its own records with its Patch Tuesday updates, including over 1,400 fixes with its October update. The company's October 2025 Patch Tuesday update, by comparison, included fewer than 180 fixes.

It's important to understand that just about every company that develops software is furiously working to patch its systems before hackers or AI agents exploit vulnerabilities first. And while there are successes (Microsoft is now protecting its customers from thousands of flaws each month), this speed is also inadvertently breaking things along the way. That's not just speculation: According to The Washington Sun, both Wall Street executives and the NSA explained to members of Congress that patching security flaws discovered by AI models caused this week's widespread outages.

Barring some campaign to cover up a coordinated attack on systems and services, it does seem like these outages are simply the result of companies breaking their own products in an attempt to stop AI-assisted hackers from exploiting undiscovered flaws. But that's not all that reassuring, either. AI models are only going to keep getting better at finding vulnerabilities; likewise, AI agents are only improving at hacking into systems autonomously. Companies will need to ramp up their efforts to patch their software before both hackers and AI agents discover those flaws first, and so the cycle will continue. Unless something changes, we may see routine outages as companies try to fix things as quickly as possible.

The implications aren't specific to any one company, either. Our world increasingly relies on fewer companies to keep us all connected. We saw that last year, when cloud hosting providers like AWS and Cloudflare each experienced outages. When these services go down, so do all of the networks that rely on them. If AWS or Cloudflare break something while trying to patch their systems, whole parts of the internet go dark.

Of course, it'll only be more difficult for the general public—if not the developers themselves—to recognize when outages are the result of maintenance or a cyberattack. Just because recent outages don't appear to be nefarious in nature, that doesn't mean future outages will be so innocent. For the time being, however, it seems we can worry less about an active cybersecurity incident, and more about how AI is disrupting modern life in ways few of us saw coming.

#3283. The 8 Best Tom Clancy Books, Ranked

Tom Clancy was one of the most successful writers of his era, with over 100 million books sold worldwide. He's also one with a very particular recipe: his stories are usually geopolitical thrillers packed with military hardware, intelligence operations, political maneuvering, and uncomfortably plausible international crises.

Submarines, nuclear weapons, special forces, and international diplomacy are the key ingredients, all rendered with obsessive attention to detail. However, the best of the author's books combine all that with high-tension plotting and characters we actually care about. Here are some of the finest, ranked.

“The difference between fiction and reality? Fiction has to make sense.” Rather than depending primarily upon battlefield action, this one leans harder into pure espionage, building tension around information. At the center is CARDINAL, a highly placed American intelligence asset inside the Soviet Union who is becoming increasingly vulnerable. Jack Ryan becomes deeply involved in the attempt to protect CARDINAL's secrecy while Soviet intelligence officers work to uncover the leak.

Clancy's detailed understanding of intelligence procedure is a big part of what makes the book work. Thanks to his research and detail, a compromised communication or suspicious pattern of behavior can be every bit as dangerous as a gunfight. Refreshingly, The Cardinal of the Kremlin also gives its Soviet characters motives and internal conflicts rather than treating the Cold War as a simple contest between interchangeable villains and heroes.

"Ryan had learned long before that people did not think clearly when they were afraid.” Patriot Games gets unusually personal. In it, Ryan is visiting London with his family when he stumbles into an attempted kidnapping involving members of the royal family. His instinctive intervention saves lives, but puts him directly in the path of a violent splinter group. Soon, Ryan is trying to protect his wife and daughter after his actions make his family a target.

Clancy builds this into a classic story of a good man up against dastardly foes, anchored by a protagonist with a moral code. The early sections also spend time letting us get to know Ryan's family and understand the bond between them, which makes sure the emotional stakes hit hard later. The plot is also handled briskly, keeping the pages flying by the whole way through.

“The only way to prevent war is to make sure that everyone understands what war means.” The Sum of All Fears gets unsettlingly plausible with its take on nuclear risks. Here, neither superpower actually wants an atomic showdown, but circumstances make them believe the other does. The plot kicks into gear after a missing Israeli nuclear weapon turns up just as peace talks seem poised to deliver a breakthrough. For Jack Ryan, now CIA deputy director, the timing could hardly be worse.

Relations between Washington and Moscow are deteriorating, and a Palestinian terrorist group sees the bomb as a way to set the two superpowers against each other. In other words, this setup takes recognizable geopolitical tensions and pushes them to the brink of World War III. However, Clancy's signature recipe of technical detail and outsize plotting ensures that the final product is still a fun thriller.

“The end does not justify the means. There are no ends, only means.” Clear and Present Danger places Ryan in conflict not only with America's enemies but with decisions being made inside his own government. After Colombian drug traffickers murder an American official and his family, powerful figures within the administration authorize a covert campaign against the cartels, and even Ryan himself is kept out of the loop.

American light infantry teams are secretly inserted into Colombia, where they begin targeting the infrastructure supporting the drug trade. Domingo "Ding" Chavez and John Clark (a character sometimes described as "Ryan's dark side") play major roles in the operation​​​​​​, making this a great Ryan/Clark crossover episode. That setup also allows Clancy to explore the moral complications of covert warfare while still delivering the military and intelligence detail his readers expect.

“Safety is something that happens between your ears, not something you hold in your hands.” Speaking of John Clark, the character finally takes center stage in Rainbow Six, which shifts attention away from Jack Ryan's political ascent and toward international counterterrorism. Clark commands Rainbow, a newly created multinational unit composed of elite operators. Soon, the team is up against a group of extremists plotting biological terrorism on a staggering scale, motivated by an ideology that regards humanity as expendable.

At 740 pages, Rainbow Six is a substantial thriller even by Clancy’s standards. However, some of the characters could still use more depth even with all that screen time, and the villains’ scheme sometimes sounds like something out of a second-tier Bond adventure. That said, the sheer number of gripping action sequences makes up for a lot, and the book spawned a video game franchise for a reason.

“John Kelly had known death before.” This gem is the original story for John Clark (aka John Kelly), and it's noticeably darker and more personal than most of Clancy's geopolitical epics. Essentially, it explains how a regular Navy SEAL is forged into the CIA’s deadliest black-ops agent. Set during the Vietnam War, the novel cuts between two missions. In one, Clark hunts down the drug dealers who killed his girlfriend.

In the other, he joins a secret operation to bring home American prisoners of war held in Vietnam. Taken together, these storylines make for what might be Clancy's strongest character portrait. Clark’s grief and moral convictions dictate the course of the story, and his doubts give him a depth that few of the author’s other protagonists enjoy. Clancy himself described the book as an inquiry into what justice means and how it should be carried out.

“Wars are begun by frightened men.” This is one of the very few Clancy books not set in the Ryanverse, but it's still a banger. Here, a Soviet fuel crisis sets the stage for a surprise invasion of Western Europe as Moscow tries to secure its oil supply. The attack draws NATO and the Warsaw Pact into an all-out war fought across land, sea, and air, but purely with conventional weapons. No nukes involved.

The book swaps out larger-than-life heroes for a multi-front look at how a Third World War might actually look. Indeed, we see the conflict from numerous perspectives: frontline tank commanders, frigate captains, fighter pilots, Kremlin strategists, and more. Submarines stalk one another beneath the Atlantic, aircraft battle for control of European skies, NATO forces attempt to hold back Soviet armor, and Iceland becomes strategically vital to control of the North Atlantic.

“Listen, I don't have to know why. I have to know what.” The Hunt for Red October introduced the world to Jack Ryan and put Clancy on the literary map, eventually becoming a killer movie, too. At the start of the book, Soviet submarine commander Marko Ramius takes the technologically advanced Red October to sea and appears to be heading toward the United States. The Americans need to determine whether he's preparing to attack them or attempting to defect. That uncertainty drives almost the entire novel.

Ryan becomes convinced that Ramius intends to hand the submarine over to the US, but he has to persuade his bosses of that while both American and Soviet forces search for Red October. From here, we get a depiction of submarine warfare that's rigorously detailed and yet still incredibly suspenseful. It mostly involves people listening, calculating, waiting, and trying to infer an opponent's intentions from incomplete information.

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

Netflix has a packed slate to end the year, including returning favorites, new films, and live events. The platform will host two Christmas Day NFL games—Bills vs. Broncos and Packers vs. Bears—as well as the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027™ Final Draw and Tyson Fury vs. Anthony Joshua on Dec. 11 and the second installment of the Six Kings Slam men's tennis tournament on Dec. 27.

On the film side, comedy Bad Day (Dec. 11) stars Cameron Diaz as a single mom having the worst day of her life in a series of comedic mishaps. THE FURTHER MIS-ADVENTURES OF CLIFF BOOTH (Dec. 23) is a crime comedy written by Quentin Tarantino, directed by David Fincher, and starring Brad Pitt as a stuntman working odd jobs in 1970s LA. The film is a spin-off (set eight years later) of the 2019 movie Once Upon a Time in Hollywood.

The December documentary lineup is long and includes 14th (Dec. 4), an Ava DuVernay film—in the spirit of the earlier 13th—that examines the 14th Amendment principles of citizenship and due process.

Finally, familiar series with new seasons include Emily in Paris (Dec. 24), My Next Guest Needs No Introduction With David Letterman (Dec. 14), and a new installment of Hot Ones: Extra Heat (Dec. 2) featuring Rob Lowe.

#3278. Taylor Swift's Alleged Mean Girl Side Exposed in Vanity Fair Profile

Taylor Swift is getting the royal treatment from Vanity Fair ... if your idea of royalty involves a queen who's allegedly got a mean streak and isn't afraid to make her enemies pay.

The magazine just dropped a scathing deep dive into the pop superstar ... but here's the kicker -- it never actually names her. Instead, the entire piece refers to Taylor as "The Star" ... although the references to friendship bracelets, her Eras Tour and husband Travis Kelce aren't exactly subtle.

The article, titled "The Mastermind" draws on interviews with more than 100 people and presents two competing versions of Taylor -- the beloved pop icon and a calculating powerhouse who allegedly punishes anyone who crosses her.

One music industry insider compares her to Regina George from "Mean Girls" ... while a former confidant claims people who fall out of favor can find themselves frozen out of her social circle.

And it doesn't stop there ... former classmates challenge Taylor's accounts of being bullied, with one even suggesting the singer was part of the popular crowd doing the bullying herself.

The piece also revisits her feud with Charli XCX, questioning whether Taylor's public support for fellow artists always matches what happens behind the scenes.

To be clear, these are allegations and opinions from the magazine's sources ... not established facts.

Vanity Fair says it sent Taylor multiple questions while reporting the story, but she declined to comment.

And while the magazine never spells out her name, it leaves plenty of Easter eggs ... in a version of Taylor's story she didn't get to write herself.

#3276. Forget 'Slow Horses,' This Sci-Fi Thriller Is Gary Oldman’s Greatest Role

If you only know Gary Oldman as the lethargic Jackson Lamb in TV hit Slow Horses, it may shock you to know that much of his career was spent bringing to life characters who were high energy, operatic, and filled every moment of screentime with their voice. There’s no greater example of this than The Fifth Element, Luc Besson’s 1997 sci-fi thriller that became an instant classic thanks to its unique vision of the future and memorable performances. As Jean-Baptiste Emanuel Zorg, a flamboyant industrialist working for the film’s evil forces, he becomes larger-than-life in the best way possible. And with the film charting among Tubi's top 10 most-watched films, now's the perfect time to revisit.

Set in the 23rd century, the film stars Bruce Willis as Korben Dallas, a New York City taxi driver and former special forces operative who is stunned when a mysterious woman named Leeloo (Milla Jovovich) falls into his cab. He learns that Leeloo is the key to fighting a great evil that is making its way toward Earth, and uniting her with stones representing the four classical elements is the only way to save humanity. With the government, as well as crazed mercenary Zorg (Oldman), on their tail, Dallas must do everything he can to save Leeloo, and become the hero he was always meant to be.

In a summer that featured dinosaurs (Jurassic Park: The Lost World), aliens (Men in Black), and kick-ass presidents (Air Force One), the French filmmaker's whimsical sci-fi tale stood out amongst traditional Hollywood fare to create a worldwide hit that retained the record for admissions in France for over a decade. The film's impact was largely due to its unique look, which captivated audiences regardless of whether they knew of Besson or understood the film's concept. Those visuals were the product of Besson collaborating with equally imaginative co-creators.

'Slow Horses' Season 5 premieres September 24 on Apple TV+.

Having made his first American-set movie with Léon: The Professional, Besson would go on to develop a story he first created when he was just 16 years old. To match his unique story, filled with prophecy, philosophy, and unknown cultures, he hired artists who would make the visuals unlike anything previously seen on the big screen. For the production design, he recruited French comic creators Jean Giraud and Jean-Claude Mézières to envision 23rd century New York City, where classic iconography met eye-popping futurism. This was symbolized by Korben Dallas’ flying yellow taxi cab, and skyscrapers that seemed to have no beginning or end.

The groundbreaking costumes, such as Leeloo’s orange suspender ensemble and the wild leopard print chic of radio host Ruby Rhod (Chris Tucker), were designed by celebrated fashion guru Jean Paul Gaultier and gave every character their own unique style. Besson already knew how to tell a compelling action story, having built his name on movies such as La Femme Nikita and Subway. By bringing in these iconoclastic artists, he would make every frame look like a comic book come to life, giving both the sci-fi and action genres a new perspective.

The counter to Willis’ sardonic, laid-back hero is Oldman’s Zorg, a character who doesn’t have a drop of subtlety in his blood stream. Elaborately dressed and prone to violent tantrums, Oldman plays Zorg with a manic intensity that borders on cartoonish. Parading around his premises like an emperor, he tries to dominate everyone he comes across, betraying his cowardice only when presented with an opponent he truly can’t overcome. The emotions are right on the surface, reflecting the actor’s previous collaboration with Besson in Léon: The Professional, where he played the corrupt, abusive, and unhinged police officer Norman Stansfield.

In a film where the effects could easily dominate proceedings, Oldman's magnetic presence becomes one of the film’s highlights. As well as giving a human face to the threat Dallas faces, he also provides a villain that feels right at home in the gaudy excess of the future that Besson brings us. A vain capitalist who is used to everything going his way, there is something in his portrayal of a powerful man with deep-seated insecurities that will resonate with today’s society as much as it did in 1997.

The mark of a great actor is the ability to tell a story in multiple ways, and Gary Oldman has made a career of sidestepping expectations. Jean-Baptiste Emanuel Zorg could not be further away from Jackson Lamb, and yet both characters showcase the commitment and ability of a star who can find a way to become part of whatever world he finds himself in. If you’ve just finished the latest season of the Apple TV hit and can’t wait for the next, check out this cult classic to see just how far your favorite spy’s range can stretch.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

Typically, Apple would release its x.2 software updates in December, but this year is different because iOS 27.1 was exclusive to iPhone Duo. That means that, in terms of the timeline, iOS 27.3 is essentially the equivalent of iOS 27.2.

Here’s when Apple has released its December updates in recent years:

So with that in mind, we expect iOS 27.3 to be released sometime during the first half of December.

The redesigned Health app is back in iOS 27.3. This was first available during testing of iOS 27.2, but did not ship as part of that final update.

The redesigned Health app is split into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The app features an all-new design that dynamically adapts based on your data, including Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab includes a new Health age feature that uses Apple Watch data to show how your metrics track relative to your actual age.

For Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 users, it also offers easy access to view your Readiness score every morning.

For Apple Fitness+, iOS 27.3 adds a new Gym Strength feature. This creates progressive, four-week plans based on your strength goals, experience, schedule, and available equipment.

As you complete each week of workouts, the following week adapts based on the reps and weights you logged.

For iPhone Duo users, iOS 27.3 adds Reachability support. This setting shifts the interface on the outer display to the right or left, making it easier to reach the far corners. It’s designed to make iPhone Duo easier to use with one hand, despite the wider outer display. You activate it by swiping right on the right edge of the screen or left on the left edge.

Reachability for iPhone Duo is on by default. You can turn it off in Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability.

iOS 27.3 also brings a new face unlock feature to iPhone Duo. This is not full-fledged Face ID. Instead, Apple is using the front-facing camera on the iPhone Duo’s outer display to recognize you, then unlock the device. It doesn’t work for things like Apple Pay and passwords.

iOS 27.3 also tweaks the iPhone Duo’s software keyboard by making the keys slightly narrower and the font slightly smaller.

Finally, iOS 27.3 includes a new option in the Settings app to have your iPhone Duo lock when closed. Once enabled, your iPhone Duo will lock when you fold it, rather than transition content from the inner display to the outer display.

When it debuted, the iPhone Duo included a more robust version of StandBy with new clock faces and expanded customization options. iOS 27.3 brings the iPhone Duo’s StandBy experience to all iPhone models.

This includes the redesigned Analog and Digital Clock faces, as well as additional customization options for colors and complications. The update also adds support for Shared Albums to the Photos face.

iOS 27.3 brings several key Siri AI updates. First, the update expands Siri AI with many new capabilities across Apple apps. Apple explains:

We started rolling out these new capabilities across many Apple apps, including Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather, so users can do things like find a coffee shop they visited last week or archive files that haven’t been opened in over a year.

There are many more actions available now as examples for you to reference. To see what you can do in each app, just ask Siri AI.

With iOS 27.3, Apple is also starting to test new ways for developers to create Siri AI integrations for the first time. This is described as an “early Developer Preview.” Apple explains:

Today’s preview allows any app to bring its content and actions directly into Siri AI by using App Intents, making it easier for all apps to tap into Siri AI’s newest capabilities, including personal context understanding, onscreen awareness, natural language, and more. So people can just ask for help in their own words, and Siri AI carries out any custom action you’ve built, from checking a delivery to booking a reservation to placing an order.

While this is being tested as part of iOS 27.3, Apple says it will start shipping to customers in a few months.

iOS 27.3 also expands Siri AI to new languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish.

iOS 27.3 also introduces usage limits on select Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features. The limits apply to things like:

You can unlock higher usage limits with an eligible iCloud+ plan, starting at $2.99 per month. If you hit your usage limit, basic Siri requests will still work. That includes things like setting timers and alarms.

iOS 27.3 brings the original set of Apple Intelligence features to China for the first time. This does not include Siri AI or other iOS 27 updates, but it does include the following features:

iOS 27.3 is a major update to Safari. First, the update adds support for a new vertical tabs design layout on iPhone Duo’s inner display. If you choose this option, your Safari tabs will be arranged vertically along the left-hand side of Safari, rather than along the top. Vertical tabs are also available on Mac and iPad with macOS 27.3 and iPadOS 27.3.

iOS 27.3 also adds a new Adaptive Dark Mode feature. This feature can automatically apply Dark Mode to websites that don’t natively support it. You can choose to have Adaptive Dark Mode automatically kick in or use it on a site-by-site basis.

For Apple Music users, iOS 27.3 adds a new “Selfie Sing” feature that lets users record a video of themselves while singing karaoke. To use this feature, start playing a song and go to the lyrics view. Then tap the new camera button that appears on the right-hand side of the lyrics.

The update also refines the design of viewing lyrics while your iPhone is in landscape mode.

There are two key changes to the Apple TV app in iOS 27.3. First, the update introduces video podcasts in the TV app. You can now watch your favorite video podcasts in the TV app, and sync your playback progress between the TV app and the Podcasts app.

Second, iOS 27.3 adds vertical video to the TV app. The app now includes a new “Explore Clip Collections” section where you can browse clips from Apple TV content in a TikTok-style design.

Here are a few other changes in iOS 27.3:

What are your favorite new features in iOS 27.3? Have you spotted any other changes in the update? Let us know down in the comments.

Delicious food, great golf and a few days in paradise

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

As a golf writer, I get to play at some pretty incredible courses. The USGA brought me out to Winged Foot to check out its new app, and it was one of the most incredible golf experiences I've ever had.

But when I received an invite to Mexico to experience Gourmet and Golf at Punta Mita, I almost fell out of my chair with excitement. I've never been to Mexico, and I've never played golf outside of the United States, so going was a no-brainer.

And I made the right decision in more ways than one. Yes, the golf was great, but this event completely changed my life for the better. Seriously.

I attended the 15th anniversary of Punta Mita's Gourmet and Golf, which led the resorts (St. Regis Punta Mita Resort and the Four Seasons Resort Punta Mita) to go a little crazy with the number and quality of chefs. But any year you go, the food and golf will be incredible, and I personally can't wait to see how good the event is for its 20th anniversary.

If you decide to attend, you're looking at $3,599 for a 3-night package and $4,399 for the four-night (I did three, and it was enough time to play two rounds of golf and eat until I felt I might pop). This includes a beautiful place to stay, all ultra-high-end meals, participation in the Punta Mita Golf Cup over 2 days at both Jack Nicklaus Signature Golf Courses, transportation to and from the airport, and more.

It's not cheap, but the value is there — how often do you get to indulge in three days of top-of-the-line food and two days of premium Jack Nicklaus Signature Golf (with one day playing out as a two-person scramble and one as a best ball event)?

This feels weird to say for me after 40 years of being overwhelmingly picky, but I was a super picky eater. Saying "was" just doesn't feel right, but going to Gourmet and Golf actually helped me break out of my picky-eating habits.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Sure, it's only been a couple of weeks, and I have to keep the momentum going by continuing to try new foods, but I feel confident saying I was a picky eater, not that I am one.

I figured that since Gourmet and Golf features some of the world's best chefs, it would be the perfect chance to let my guard down and try whatever was put in front of me. So I did. I tried foods that would normally make me recoil in fear. I ate caviar, tacos and things I can't even pronounce; things I don't even remember. I tried shrimp, lobster and other foods I've had in the past and didn't like. I confirmed I still don't like them, but I tried them without hesitation.

It was like a food blur, and just about everything I tried was great. I counted for the first couple of days of the trip, but eventually the whirlwind of new foods became too much. I'd guess I tried at least 40 new foods.

If you're a picky eater like me, Gourmet and Golf could change your approach to food if you let it. And if you're not a picky eater (like my girlfriend Andria, who accompanied me on the trip), then you're in for a treat, because the food is some of the best you can get. There's a reason these are Michelin-starred chefs — they know what they're doing.

Okay, so the food was good. It changed my life and helped me overcome my fear of trying new foods. Good for me, right? But how were the Nicklaus-designed Bahia and Pacifico golf courses?

I keep track of my golf course ratings on a cool app called Eden. In it, Winged Foot West is my number one course — it gets 10 on my rating scale. Now, though, it has another course nipping at its heels, with the Pacifico course at Punta Mita getting a 9.9. And it's close — while ranking the courses, I actually considered putting Punta Mita above Winged Foot West based primarily on the blend of incredible vistas and the overall quality of the golf.

In the end, the history and legacy offered by Winged Foot gave it a slight edge, but it's close. And the Bahia course isn't far behind, coming in as the 7th best course I've ever played (beaten by Winged Foot West, Tamarack Country Club, Pacifico, Country Club of Waterbury, Scottsdale National and PGA National). Between the two courses, Punta Mita is clearly a destination with golfers in mind.

To give you an idea of some of the other courses with the Nicklaus pedigree, we're talking about The Saint Andrews Golf Club, Great Bear Golf Club, Bayside, Champion Course at PGA National, Harbour Town Golf Links, Nicklaus Course at PGA West and the list goes on and on. Punta Mita's golf courses come with some serious pedigree, and they live up to the challenge for which Nicklaus is known.

Which would explain why I shot a 115 during the best ball portion of the tournament.

These are hard golf courses designed to test every aspect of your golf game with massive, intelligently placed bunkers, narrow fairways, undulating greens, false fronts and all the other tricks that rack up strokes.

But nothing about the design feels haphazard or just there to make things difficult. It's all built to reward smart course management and good shots — something I was apparently incapable of during this particular trip (to give you some perspective, I typically shoot in the mid-to-upper 90s, so I shot almost 20 strokes more than normal).

You know what? I don't care. My partner didn't care. It's hard to care what you shoot when you're surrounded by such beautiful scenery, like you are on both the Bahia and Pacifico courses at Punta Mita. And when the round was over, I knew I had some of the best culinary delights I've ever experienced waiting for me (and strategically placed around the two courses).

It doesn't matter what you shoot; you will have a good time at Gourmet and Golf. Just ask my partner — she didn't even play golf and can't stop talking about going back for another year.

#3265. Gavin Newsom Blasted By Mother of Murdered 8-Year-Old After Commuting Death Row Sentences

Gavin Newsom was raked over the coals by the mother of a murdered 8-year-old and several other family members of victims after he commuted the sentences of all of California's death row inmates.

Here's the deal ... earlier this month, Governor Newsom commuted all 548 death row inmates -- changing their punishment from death to life in prison.

President Donald Trump, looking to shame the governor for his choice, hosted family members of several victims at an event Monday ... at which he called out Newsom for standing with "the murderers and the child slayers."

The prez then handed off the mic to Sandy Friend ... whose 8-year-old son Michael Lyons was sexually assaulted, tortured and killed by Robert Boyd Rhoades in 1996.

Rhoades was sentenced to death, but it was never carried out ... and the commutation means he will now serve a life sentence instead.

At the podium, Sally spoke directly to Newsom ... saying, "Face me, Governor Newsom. Tell me Michael’s life doesn’t matter. Michael deserved a governor who would stand with the victims, honor their justice, and respect the will of the people.”

Other victims -- including the family of a slain police detective and the father of 12-year-old Polly Klaas, who was strangled to death in 1996 -- also ripped into the governor.

It's worth noting ... the last time a California inmate was executed was 2006 -- though California voters chose not to abolish it at least twice since then.

In a statement to the New York Post, Governor Newsom said, "To the families standing with him today: your grief is real. Every person on California’s former death row will die in prison. Not one walks out. Donald Trump’s criminals walk out.”

Apple TV (now $6.99/month for limited time) has just unveiled the return of one of its most popular series: Presumed Innocent. Here’s the release date and first trailer.

Here’s the official plot summary, followed by the teaser trailer:

The sophomore season of “Presumed Innocent” is based on “Dissection of a Murder,” the debut legal thriller novel by Jo Murray, who also serves as a co-executive producer. Up-and-coming defense attorney Lelia Reynolds (Brosnahan) faces off against her district attorney husband (Rhys) in a murder case that threatens to destroy both their careers and their marriage.

You can watch Presumed Innocent season 1 on Apple TV. The eight-episode first season tells the story of “the horrific murder that upends the Chicago Prosecuting Attorney’s office when one of its own is suspected of a crime.”

Apple has started making a habit of renewing shows that were originally intended as limited series.

Zosia says her sister told her, "It's not fair! Everybody else's 80-year-old dad loves Trump, but they're not famous."

Zosia says she ultimately still loves her dad ... adding he's a great hang -- and definitely one of the smartest people she knows.

With Thanksgiving right around the corner, it's nice to know even celebs might have some awkward political chats around the table this holiday season!

#3260. Apple’s ‘just works’ approach is great, but goes a little too far

“It just works” is one of the phrases most commonly associated with Apple. Interestingly, it appears to have been coined by the company’s customers and then used by reviewers before it was later picked up by Steve Jobs.

Of course, it’s now commonly used ironically when Apple products don’t do what they are supposed to (Apple Home, I’m looking at you), but I do think that it’s absolutely the right philosophy and goal – most of the time …

Macworld referenced an Apple brochure from 1996 entitled “Why do people prefer Macintosh?” This is a collection of testimonials from customers, a number of whom use the “it just works” phrasing. It was subsequently used by a number of reviewers. The earliest example I can find of Steve Jobs adopting it was in 1999, when discussing the rollout of FireWire to the Mac in the PowerMac G3.

It’s hot-pluggable. You don’t have to turn your computer off to connect and disconnect peripherals, you can just plug them right in. Again, the drivers are dynamically loaded. There are no terminators and there are no switches. It just works.

(If you have a link to any earlier example, please do let me know in the comments.)

I’m a big fan of the philosophy. Most of the time, users should just be able to get on with the tasks they want to execute without having to worry about the technology. The tech that makes it all possible should sit there quietly in the background.

However, there are cases where I think Apple takes this approach a little too far, and where tech-savvy users at least would like a little more transparency and control.

AirPods firmware updates are a good example. Back in September, there was quite a significant update in the form of custom EQ. It’s a rather basic version, but still a feature many had wanted for a long time. Instead of being able to manually trigger the update, users had to wait until it “just worked.”

Apple’s support document has a how-to guide that is essentially an outline of the conditions required to permit an update, and an instruction to simply wait until it happens. Which you will only know by repeatedly checking.

Make sure your AirPods are connected via Bluetooth to your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Connect your charging case to a power source. Put your AirPods in their charging case and close the lid. Keep the lid of the charging case closed, and keep your AirPods in Bluetooth range of your iPhone, iPad or Mac. Wait at least 30 minutes for the firmware to be updated. Check the firmware version again.

Another example, and one I’ve complained about before, is that there is no way to manually trigger an iCloud document sync, nor any progress indicator when it does finally happen. In the best of cases, it takes seconds; in the worst, many hours. And again, the only way to find out is to repeatedly check.

It’s the same story when shooting a video on your iPhone. Will it still be there an hour later, available to instantly edit and view? Maybe, or maybe it will have been offloaded to the cloud, requiring it to be downloaded before you can do anything with it – while a video you shot months earlier is still stored locally on the device! You can, of course, switch off optimization altogether, but if you choose to use it, you get no control over it. I want a setting that allows me to do things like specify local retention of all photos and videos taken within the past fortnight.

Will that video be available in the Mac Photos app when you check half an hour later? Maybe, maybe not. You can click the Sync Now button as many times as you like, and it will apparently have no effect, claiming it’s up to date despite the video being entirely absent. It will be there when it’s there.

Once it is in the Photos app on your Mac, it’s a similar story when exporting it to a folder. You can drag and drop the video into the folder, and this time you are manually triggering the transfer (yay!), but there will be absolutely no visual indication that it is in progress. No grayed-out icon, no progress bar, nothing. So far as the user interface is concerned, it appears that your drag and drop had no effect – until the video file finally appears.

I think with all of these things and more, Apple needs to offer options. Yes, most non-tech users may be perfectly happy to just wait until things happen, but there ought to be a standard way to trigger things that currently happen in their own sweet time, as well as progress indicators and confirmation that a process is complete.

Is this an ecosystem-wide improvement you’d like to see? Please share your thoughts in the comments and add any frustrating examples of your own.

The kit includes a base station, keypad, entry sensors, a motion sensor, and a panic button, so you can monitor doors, windows, and movement inside the house. The Arlo Home Security System is $142.49, down from $199.99, and this starter kit pairs a Keypad Sensor Hub with two All-in-One Sensors, each of which can be set to detect motion, open doors and windows, water leaks, and other events across eight functions. Arlo’s Essential Pan Tilt Indoor Cam 2K is $18.99, down from $49.99, and it’s part of the lineup Arlo released in 2025, with a motorized head that rotates a full 360 degrees and tilts 180 degrees so one camera can cover an entire room. This PCMag review goes into more detail on how it performs.

The Sensi Smart Thermostat ST55 is currently $79, down from $129.99, and is a good option for anyone looking to control their home's heating and cooling from a phone—it lets you create schedules, adjust temperatures remotely, and use geofencing to make changes based on whether you're home or away. The Amazon Smart Thermostat is a more affordable alternative at $56.99, down from $79.99. The Roborock Qrevo CurvX has dropped to $799.99 from $1,499.99, saving you $700. Why fight for the TV when you can have a big-screen GTA 6 experience right on your face?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

After 13 long years, the wait is finally over, and like many of you, I couldn’t wait to load up GTA 6 for the first time this weekend. However, instead of playing on the largest screen in my house, I decided that a pair of AR glasses might be the best way to experience this new and improved Vice City. Let me explain.

With a game this massive and this anticipated, the last thing you want is to be interrupted — or worse, unable to play because someone else in your household claimed the TV first. Now, if you’re an adult who lives by yourself and got to play GTA 6 sprawled out on your couch with one of the best OLED TVs, more power to you.

For those of us with a significant other or kids at home, though, carving out the necessary time to finally play GTA 6 hasn’t been that easy. Fortunately for me, I knew there was another way instead of trying to sneak in a late-night play session in front of the TV.

You see, over the summer on a trip to Taiwan for Computex, I spent almost my entire 17-hour flight playing Red Dead Redemption on the Switch 2 in AR glasses. That got me thinking: what if I tried playing GTA 6 the same way? Well, that’s exactly what I did, and I don’t think I’d be nearly as far in the game right now if I hadn’t.

Here’s why you, too, might want to consider donning a pair of AR glasses—or more accurately, display glasses — to take in the sights, sounds, and excitement that Vice City has to offer in GTA 6.

This bundle has everything you need to start playing your game consoles in AR. You get a pair of Viture Pro 2 XR glasses and the Viture Pro Mobile Dock. This way you can plug your Switch 2 in directly over USB-C or consoles like the PS5 or Xbox Series X in over HDMI and the included dock brings big-screen console gaming right to your glasses. Alternatively, if you only plan on playing your Switch 2 this way, you can pick up the Viture Pro 2 Mini Dock Pack for $375 (down from $428) right now.

With a gaming PC or even a handheld like the Steam Deck, playing with AR glasses is as simple as plugging them in. On a console, though, it’s not that easy. Fortunately, Viture makes a few accessories to help.

For instance, there’s the Viture Pro Mobile Dock and the new Viture Mobile Dock Mini. While I played RDR using the latter, when I tried playing my Switch 2 in AR glasses back at launch, I used the former. Don’t get me wrong, the new mini dock is super compact and easier to bring with you, but for playing on any console besides the Nintendo Switch, it’s missing one very important port: HDMI.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Now with the Pro Mobile Dock, in addition to USB-C out ports for two pairs of glasses — and a USB-C input for devices like the Switch 2 — you also get a full-sized HDMI port. Admittedly, I didn’t have a use for it before as I’ve mainly played games in AR glasses while traveling or on vacation, but with my PS5 Pro fired up with GTA 6 installed and ready to go, it was time to put it to the test.

I ran a long HDMI cable from the back of my console, plugged it into the dock along with a pair of the Viture Pro 2 AR glasses, powered it on, and I was good to go. GTA 6 appeared almost instantly on the Micro-OLED displays in the glasses, and since they have built-in speakers, that was all I needed.

Although I love their more affordable $299 price, Viture did have to cut one of my favorite features from its other glasses. Unlike the company’s other models — and this is true with the Xreal XBX A01 glasses, too — there isn’t any built-in electrochromic dimming. Instead, you get a lens shade in the box.

Now, if you’ve never worn a pair of AR glasses before, electrochromic dimming lets you go from a clear display where you can see the world around you (in addition to the content from your game console, phone, or tablet) to a dimmed one without ambient light seeping through, all with the push of a button.

The Viture Pro 2 glasses do have one feature going for them that made my GTA 6 play sessions a whole lot more comfortable, though. They’re extremely lightweight at just 63 grams.

Playing GTA 6 with AR glasses felt just like making my way through the Wild West as John Marston in RDR. I was able to take in all of Leonida without bothering anyone else in my house, and since the game runs at 30 fps, I didn’t lose anything when it came to visual quality. Now, if I were playing on PC, that would be a different story, since the Pro 2s come equipped with a 120Hz refresh rate — making them just as good for fast-paced games as they are for slower ones.

If you want to try something similar, you’ll get the best experience using the Pro Mobile Dock — or better yet, Viture’s new HDMI to USB-C adapter cable. Mine is still in the mail, though, so I made do with the Pro Mobile Dock, and for now, everything worked exceptionally well. However, that isn’t the only way to play GTA 6 in AR glasses.

Besides using Viture’s AR glasses with one of its docks, I’ve also spent a fair amount of time playing on a smartphone, too. If you have a newer iPhone, Samsung phone, or any smartphone with DisplayPort Alt Mode over USB-C, you just plug your glasses in and you’re good to go. With that kind of setup, you can load up a remote play app like PXPlay (for PlayStation) or XBXPlay (for Xbox) and use a wireless controller.

That does leave your phone just lying there, which is why Viture teamed up with 8BitDo a while back to create a variant of the 8BitDo Ultimate Mobile Gaming Controller with a full-featured USB-C port. On most mobile game controllers, the USB-C ports are just used for passthrough charging. With this one, though, you can plug in a pair of AR glasses and actually get video out.

Just like I did during my second long-haul flight to Taiwan a few years back, I popped my Samsung Galaxy S24 FE into the controller and plugged in my AR glasses. After getting PXPlay set up on that phone, I was able to use remote play on my PS5 Pro to play GTA 6 in bed.

As I was fixing up Jason’s house, though, I noticed that it was slightly difficult to see and read the button prompts on the edges of the screen. Since this was my first time playing GTA 6, I had no idea which button to press when using a nail gun to hang drywall or to fix the shingles on my roof. So I put the Pro 2s down and switched to the Viture Luma Pro glasses instead.

With the simple mission of giving you the best bang for your buck in AR glasses, Viture knocked it out the park with Luma Pro. These have the best color science of any glasses on this list, and there’s versatility in the Spacewalker software to turn any space into a giant 152-inch panoramic workspace with 3DoF tracking that keeps it anchored.

With their higher-resolution lenses (from 1080p per eye to 1200p), wider field of view (from 46 to 52 degrees), and redesigned optical stack, what was blurry on the Pro 2s became instantly clear on the Luma Pros. Now, if you’re on a tight budget and already know the controls, you can still definitely play GTA 6 with the Pro 2s. However, since I was new to the controls and had both pairs of glasses handy, making the switch was easy and absolutely worthwhile.

One feature that you’ll find on both pairs of glasses — and pretty much the rest of the AR glasses in Viture’s lineup — are myopia dials. With these, you can turn the dials to go from a blurry to a clear picture if, like me, you wear glasses or contacts. Most of the time I wear contacts, and I make it a point to have them in when wearing AR glasses. However, since I wanted to play in bed, I decided this was finally the time to try them out.

Now, I had to fully light the room in the pictures above, but on Friday and Saturday — and hopefully on Sunday evening once I’m done writing this — I cozied up in bed with that special 8BitDo controller and my AR glasses and played more GTA 6 than I’d like to admit. And frankly, it was awesome.

At first, I was a bit worried about the remote play experience with such a complex game, but with one of the best mesh Wi-Fi systems equipped with Wi-Fi 7 and a fast internet connection, it worked really well.

Now, I did have my PS5 Pro plugged into my router with an Ethernet cable during those play sessions. However, when I took the pics above, I had it unplugged, and that tanked the game’s performance. So if you want to play GTA 6 remotely — with or without AR glasses — I strongly recommend connecting your console over Ethernet for a smoother and more stable remote play experience.

As I’m also currently testing out the Viture Pro Neckband, I decided to put it on and go play outside for a bit of fun. While the device around my neck might look like a wearable fan, it’s actually a wearable Android tablet, if you can believe it.

Now, what I like about this setup compared to using the Pro Mobile Dock or a smartphone is that my hands weren’t weighed down and I wasn’t tethered to my console. Likewise, if you’re using a third-party app like PXPlay, you can use whatever controller you want and aren’t limited to just using a wired DualSense (like you are on PC).

Now, I must say that playing GTA 6 wasn’t nearly as good on the Pro Neckband as it was on a smartphone. Still, with my Eero Outdoor 7 mesh node on the fence behind me and seated in The Foldable Gaming Chair, it was quite comfy and still very playable. If only the weather had been Vice City sunny instead of overcast.

With a pair of AR glasses and the right dock — or even a capable smartphone — the possibilities are really endless. You’re not just limited to sitting in front of your TV or, if you have kids like I do, playing at your desk. On that second point, I haven’t seen anything too spicy — except for Mandy in a bikini — just yet, but given this is Grand Theft Auto after all, I know it’s coming. I wouldn’t want my son or my wife walking in on something inappropriate on my TV, and by playing with AR glasses on, I don’t have to worry about it.

Now, I know AR glasses, or display glasses, aren’t a must-have gadget like a smartphone, but they make for a very useful accessory. While they’re amazing on planes — and trust me, I’ve put in quite a lot of hours gaming or even watching movies with them aboard an aircraft — they’re just as useful and convenient at home.

As for me, it’s time to get back to Vice City and enjoy the quiet, slow-paced life of Chapter 1 before I eventually have to go pick up Lucia from prison.

#3253. Apple Calendar got two feature upgrades it really needed in iOS 27

Apple Calendar keeps getting better, including some design updates coming in iOS 27.3. But there are two standout feature upgrades added recently in iOS 27 that Apple’s Calendar app really needed.

I’ve used Apple’s Calendar app for years, and there’s an elegant simplicity to it. But one key area the app has long lagged behind competitors is event creation.

When you need to create a new event, the Calendar app historically has required manually filling in various fields for the title, date, time, invitees, etc. By contrast, the excellent third-party app Fantastical lets you type in natural language and it automatically fills in relevant parameters based on what you type.

In iOS 27, Apple finally introduces its own natural language input for Calendar events. You can type out your event details and certain recognized parameters will be used to automatically fill in the detail fields.

While the feature still isn’t on par with what Fantastical offers, since it doesn’t support as many data points as the third-party alternative, it’s very much a step in the right direction.

Apple has always pitched Siri as being like a personal assistant. As such, calendar-related tasks should have been Siri’s strong suit. But until iOS 27, you couldn’t actually manage your calendar very well using Siri.

With Siri AI, that’s changed in a big way. Now, you can do things like:

One of my favorite personal examples is from this summer when the NFL schedule was released. I asked Siri to find the Dallas Cowboys schedule and add every game to my calendar, and it pulled this off with ease.

Siri is so much better than before at assisting with your calendar, and iOS 27.3 will bring even more capabilities soon.

What are your favorite iOS 27 Apple Calendar upgrades? Let us know in the comments.

#3252. Six Things You Should Do Now to Optimize Your Setup for GTA 6

You’re almost ready for Grand Theft Auto VI. You’ve preloaded the game on your console, you’ve taken the next month off work, and you’ve locked your phone in a Faraday cage and set it adrift at sea. You’re prepared to lock in, and you haven’t forgotten a thing…right? Well, just to make sure, here are the most important tips to optimize your setup before you fire up the most anticipated game of the decade.

GTA 6 is absurdly large. According to Rockstar, you’ll need up to 212GB of storage space. For high-end consoles like the PS5 Pro, that’s more than 10% of the available storage space, and close to half the space on the more budget-conscious Xbox Series S. There’s a good chance you’ll have to delete something to make room.

Alternatively, it’s pretty easy to add more storage (if you can afford it). External SSDs are probably the cheapest route, though you’ll want to make sure to use a high-speed USB cable to connect it. It’s even worth shopping around for alternate models of SSD. For example, at the time of writing, the popular 2TB WD_BLACK external drive was close to $200, but the exact same drive in pink was $132.

You can also directly upgrade the storage of your console with expansion drives. The Xbox Series X|S supports proprietary expansion cards, while the PS5 and PS5 Pro can accept most M.2 internal SSDs. These will generally be faster, since they plug directly into the console via higher-speed connections than a drive hooked up via USB.

Let’s face it: Half the fun of any sandbox game is the weird, unique stuff that happens to only you. So you’re probably going to be hitting that “record recent gameplay” button more often than usual. While you’re cleaning up your storage space (or adding more), make sure to account for all the video clips you might want to save.

File size of video clips depends on a lot of factors, but 4K recordings can generally take up to 0.5GB per minute of footage. You can cut that down by saving footage in 1080p instead, but either way you’ll want to leave a little extra space.

Game footage is also a pretty good place to look if you need to make room on your console and don’t want to delete any games. Be honest with yourself: You don’t need all those clips from Horizon Forbidden West you saved four years ago. Dive into the settings on your console and find the biggest media files you forgot you even had on there.

According to Rockstar, GTA 6 will be targeting 30fps across consoles at launch, which is pretty low as modern AAA games go. Part of the reason for that is all the processing power going to rendering a complex environment, but it also means you won’t need a fancy high frame rate TV or monitor any time soon to get the most out of it. Still, it couldn’t hurt to check a few settings on your display.

First, make sure you’re using a higher refresh rate than 30Hz. While the game is targeting 30fps, it is technically capable of more, so if your console can keep up, you don’t want to accidentally bottleneck your frames. This setting will vary by device, so check the manual that came with your screen.

Also, make sure you have HDR enabled on your hardware. There’s a good chance this is already turned on for your TV, but sometimes other devices can switch display modes if they only support SDR. The game will help you calibrate your HDR settings for GTA 6 specifically when you launch it, but only if it detects HDR compatibility in the first place.

If you’re planning to buy a console specifically for GTA 6, this might be one of those rare instances where a PS5 Pro really is worth the upgrade. According to Rockstar, certain features like ray-traced shadows will only be available on the Pro version of Sony’s console.

More importantly, the PS5 Pro version supports PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (or PSSR), which upscales lower-resolution images to get better detail and higher frame rates out of the same hardware. Given that GTA 6 is already starting at a meager target of 30fps on most consoles, anything that can give your frame rate a boost is probably going to feel like a welcome improvement over the baseline.

I’ll tell you a secret as someone who’s spent a lot of time testing different game controllers: Most of the time, you really don’t need an expensive “elite” controller. Most of the time. I don’t buy into the idea that a taller control stick is going to make you an esports athlete. It can be nice to have, but it’s not a game changer. What does matter is customizing your controls, especially for long gaming sessions.

The DualSense Edge wireless controller is a favorite of mine, mainly because of the rear paddles and adjustable triggers. The former lets you map any button to a rear lever that you can access with your fingers underneath the controller, which can often ease some of the wrist strain of awkward button combos. And the adjustable triggers let you activate the buttons with less motion, again reducing repetitive stress.

The Xbox Elite Series 2 controller has similar features for the Xbox, as well as custom caps for the D-pad. Both consoles’ versions of pro controllers are more expensive than the standard ones, but if you’re planning to game for many hours, it can be worth it to get a controller that’s more comfortable for you.

If you have an Xbox One, you don’t necessarily have to upgrade your console to play GTA 6, but you might want to take a look at your network. GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on day one, and you’ll be able to stream the game to an Xbox One console (as long as you purchase Cloud playtime as well or get some with your Game Pass subscription). This is the only way to play on a console older than the current generation, so if you don’t want to shell out for new hardware, this might be your best bet.

Xbox recommends a minimum of a 20Mbps connection to run cloud gaming, but more is obviously better. If you can connect your console to a wired Ethernet connection, that would be better and provide more stability. If you can’t connect a cable, then at least make sure you’re well within range of your wifi router, and try to limit any other bandwidth-hogging applications on the network while you’re playing.

#3250. You Can Get One of These Pocket E-Readers for As Little As $55 Before Black Friday

Black Friday is usually a great time to grab a new e-reader, but the ongoing RAM crisis has made that a question mark this year: Amazon recently raised the prices of all its Kindles by around $50 and refreshed the entire lineup, which means your odds of grabbing one at a big discount are low. But you aren't totally out of luck: If you haven't noticed, micro-e-readers—I'm talking credit card-sized, with screens that measure around four inches—are all the rage in 2026, and right now, you can pick up one of them for around $55.

If you too can see the appeal of carrying all of your books with you on a device so small you'll forget it's even in your pocket, it's a great time to jump in: The recently released Xteink X4 Classic is currently 38% off for Black Friday, bringing it down to $54.87, a record-low price. Meanwhile, the smaller X3 is $55.72, or 19% off. Both are available in either "mist grey" or "space black." The discounts should last through the end of Cyber Monday on Nov. 30.

Xteink is a Chinese startup that shook up the e-reading world last year with the launch of the X4, a super bare-bones device that made up for its lack of features and usability with a cheap sub-$70 price point. Since then, a huge online community of fans has formed, sharing tips on Reddit and even coming together to crowdsource an alternate operating system that fixed a lot of early problems. Xteink quickly followed up the X4 with a slate of other devices, including the 3.7-inch X3 and the X4 Pro, which adds a front light and touchscreen (at the cost of screen clarity and two physical buttons).

The X4 Classic and the X3 improve on the original X4 with quality-of-life upgrades like a larger battery, relocated page-turn buttons, a real-time clock, and a tilt-to-turn-page feature. They're also lighter and thinner than the X4, though there is a trade-off involved: They drop the USB-C charging port in favor of magnetic pogo pins that require a separate adapter (included).

These upgrades also increased the cost: The X4 Classic typically retails for $89, $20 more than the discontinued X4 and only $10 less than the X4 Pro, while the X3 launched at $79. But right now, the X4 Classic is just under $55, or around 38% off, and the X3 is about a dollar more. Either is a great option for those who prioritize crisp, readable text above the conveniences of a built-in light or touchscreen, as those add extra layers between the inner screen and outer glass. It's also important to understand what you're getting into: These devices support only e-books without Digital Rights Management (DRM), which means you can't use it to read your existing library of Kindle books. On the plus side, there's no longer a need to worry about flashing new firmware if you don't want to, as the native version has been totally overhauled and is now one of your best options (though the new firmware, called "Licorice," isn't available on the X3 quite yet).

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

No. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.
